title: Bloom Energy (BE): A Real Power Platform, but an Unforgiving Price
archetype: High-expectations growth with broken tactical trend
target_base_method: 10-year DCF: $4.5B FY2026 guidance midpoint; 20% revenue CAGR; FCF margin rises from 1.36% to 12%; 10% discount rate; 3% terminal growth; $0.295B net debt-like obligations; 324.289M diluted weighted-average shares.
target_bear_method: 10-year DCF: 12% revenue CAGR; FCF margin rises from 1.36% to 6%; 12% discount rate; 2.5% terminal growth; same disclosed balance-sheet obligations and diluted-share denominator.
target_bull_method: 10-year DCF: 30% revenue CAGR; FCF margin rises from 1.36% to 18%; 8% discount rate; 3% terminal growth; same disclosed balance-sheet obligations and diluted-share denominator.
holding_rationale: The ledger shows 23.526572 shares, worth $4,750.72 at the Nov 12 close, against $5,999.98 cost. The loss is $1,249.26; the weight is 5.24%. Exit is recommended: base DCF value is below the monitor band, and price sits below the 50-day and 200-day averages. The position is tactical momentum, so the broken trend removes its thesis. Schwab holds 7.2505 shares (cost $1,999.98; value $1,464.09); Robinhood holds 16.276072 (cost $4,000; value $3,286.63). The Schwab file last shows activity on Nov 10. Verify lots and live price before acting.

primer: Bloom sells solid-oxide onsite power systems, installation and long-term service. The business has real customers and rapid recent growth, but cash after factory investment remains thin, customer/project concentration is meaningful, the as-of market price discounts a demanding decade, and the technical trend is damaged. New capital is rejected; the recorded tactical position is recommended for exit.

ch4.intro_prose: The market-facts ledger is the decision anchor: Nov 12 close, daily averages, volume and Stage 1 classification. Later intraday observations are separated rather than silently mixed into the close.
ch4.gate_intro_prose: A screen can identify a monitor band; it cannot authorize a purchase when the base valuation and the trend disagree.
ch4.closing_prose: The chart and valuation both argue against adding. Treat the support band as a future observation point; re-authorize risk only after trend repair and a fresh valuation review.
ch4.stage_explanation: The Nov 12 market-facts ledger places price below both the 50-day and 200-day averages, while the 50-day remains above the 200-day; the formal ledger classification is Stage 1, not a confirmed Stage 4 cross.
ch4.evaluation_stage_explanation: Stage 1 with price below the major daily and weekly averages; no new capital until the stock builds a base and confirms a stronger trend.
ch4.posture_explanation: The Nov 12 price is below the 50-day, 200-day, 30-week and 10-week averages. A support touch is not enough; require a stable base and trend reclaim.
ch4.support_zone_explanation: Monitor-only pivot band from the as-of-aligned screen. It is not a buy zone because base DCF value is below the band.
ch4.stop_placement_explanation: Screen invalidation reference beneath the monitor band; no live stop is active because new capital is rejected and the current holding action is exit.

valuation_assessment.note: Approximate EV is $60.0B versus $4.5B FY2026 guided revenue, or 13.3x forward sales; filing-based base DCF is about $75.98/share.
